insights.title: FfprobeRunner.ResolveBinaryPath() has inverted priority order vs FfmpegRunner
insights.content: `FfprobeRunner.ResolveBinaryPath()` checks the bundled provisioner path *before* the user-configured override (`Library.FfprobePath`), the reverse of `FfmpegRunner`'s three-step order (user override → provisioner → PATH). The user's ffprobe path setting is therefore silently ignored at runtime. `FfmpegRunner` is correct; `FfprobeRunner` needs the same ordering applied. Flagged as an open item in constraints.md; a follow-up WP is required to fix it.

insights.title: Pure-unit ResolveBinaryPath tests are misplaced in the integration test suite
insights.content: The three `[Fact]` tests exercising `FfprobeRunner.ResolveBinaryPath()` (ReturnsLibraryPath_WhenLibraryPathIsSet, ReturnsProvisionerPath_WhenOnlyProvisionerPathIsSet, ReturnsFallback_WhenNeitherPathIsSet) were placed in `VideoIndexer.Infrastructure.Tests` (the integration suite) during WP-001 implementation. Since `ResolveBinaryPath()` is a pure in-memory method with no external dependencies, these tests belong in `VideoIndexer.Tests` (the unit suite). This was independently flagged by all three pipeline agents (Developer, QA, Reviewer). Move them in the next test project boundary cleanup pass. The `FfmpegRunner` may have the same gap — verify when addressing this.

insights.title: EditBookmarkCommand does not forward videoPath — Edit mode lacks frame-capture preview (deferred)
insights.content: BookmarksPanelViewModel.EditBookmarkCommand calls IBookmarkSettingsService.ShowAsync without passing _videoPath, which silently falls back to the null default. As a result, Edit mode does not offer frame-capture previews for the thumbnail field. This was intentionally deferred from WP-002 scope (noted by Developer, QA, and Reviewer). The omission looks like an oversight from the code alone; it is deliberate. Implementing Edit-mode frame capture requires threading _videoPath to the ShowAsync call inside EditBookmarkCommand in BookmarksPanelViewModel.cs.
